G1.rationale: None of the three PASS routes is documented in the extract. The compulsory core is 36 credit points of Table E foundation studies whose units are academic literacies, numeracy and essay writing (INLI1001, INLI1002, MATH1100, MATH1200, WRIT1001) — generic content without disciplinary identity. Disciplinary depth is delegated to a 48-credit-point major chosen from the Table A Subject Areas and a minor or second major drawn from a shared pool spanning eight faculty areas; the extract carries no unit table, prerequisite chain or accreditation sequence for any of them, so no all-compulsory specialist core, accredited sequence or staged prerequisite chain is evidenced. Scored on what the handbook extract documents (R1), with the ambiguity resolved down rather than up.

G2.rationale: The FAIL condition is recall or scripted responses only, and that is contradicted: a core capstone unit carries two open-ended assessments totalling 100% that require comparative critique across two knowledge paradigms, evaluation of significance, and first-hand observation, against program outcomes calling for new arguments tested against evidence and original interpretations. This is the capstone route with genuine uncertainty in the judgements required. The route's accountability element is not documented in the extract — no external host, client or defence appears — so the pass rests on the capstone's uncertainty alone, which is recorded as an ambiguity.

ambiguities: C2 straddled levels 1 and 2: reflection is genuinely assessed (20% plus 5%) and the 60% capstone portfolio names 'reflection' and 'comparative critique', which reads toward the level-2 'portfolio with standards, structured critique'; but no criteria, rubric, exemplars or peer review are documented, and the critique targets knowledge paradigms rather than the quality of work. Resolved down to 1 by the never-resolve-upward rule.

C4 straddled levels 1 and 2: CILO 1 and CILO 7 claim transfer in outcomes only, which would be level 1, but the assessed capstone portfolio requires the cross-context comparison the level-2 anchor names, so level 1's 'not assessed' clause is factually contradicted and 2 stands. Levels 2 and 3 were also weighed; 3 was refused because the capstone topic is unit-set, not self-scoped.

C5 straddled levels 1 and 2: 'first-hand sky observation' inside the capstone portfolio is primary data collection, which points at level 2, but no methodology selection or inquiry design is documented. Resolved down to 1 by the never-resolve-upward rule.

W2 straddled levels 1 and 2: the capstone's multimedia project could be read as a practitioner artefact in cultural communication, but neither an external context nor criteria drawn from practice is documented. Resolved down to 1 by the never-resolve-upward rule and R4 (no scoring up on labels).

C1 versus W1: the oral presentation with submitted work could be read into either item. Scored in W1 only, whose construct names communication to an audience; C1 scores coordination across people and tools, which the task does not document (one construct, one home).

C2 versus W2: the capstone portfolio evidence appears in both items but for different features — appraisal and reflection in C2, task fidelity in W2 — and no level was lifted in either on the strength of the other.

G2 straddled PASS and FAIL: the capstone route requires uncertainty AND accountability, and accountability is undocumented, which argues for FAIL; but the stated FAIL condition, recall or scripted responses only, is plainly contradicted by the capstone's open-ended critique tasks. PASS recorded with the accountability gap stated.
notScoreable: Four of the five documented Table E core units — INLI1002 Indigenous Literacies in Academic Contexts B, MATH1100 Power of Number A, MATH1200 Power of Number B and WRIT1001 Writing and Rhetoric: Academic Essays — carry an empty 'Assessment Tasks:' section in the extract and identical boilerplate learning-outcome wording, so no assessment evidence from them was available to any item. Assessment-based scoring rests on INLI1001 and INLI3000 alone.

The 48-credit-point major and the 36-credit-point minor or second major, which together supply 84 to 96 of the 168 credit points, have no unit list, outcomes or assessment detail in the extract. Any item that could be lifted by major-level units — C1, C2, C3, C5, W1, W2 and W3 — is therefore scored on the documented common core only, and G1 is assessed on the same limited basis.
No AI or generative-AI content of any kind appears in the extract, so C3's level-2 and level-3 anchors could not be tested against unit content; the score reflects documented digital-tool use only.
